{{Top}}
{{Citation}}
{{Quote|You astromechs think very highly of yourselves, just because you can pilot starfighters.|[[TC-16]] to R2-D2|<ref name="Labyrinth">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>}}
[[File:DSquadAstromechs-FFp58.png|thumb|right|300px|Various models of R-series astromech droids]]
An '''astromech droid''', sometimes shortened to just an '''astromech''' and also referred to as an '''astro droid''', was a type of [[Droid/Legends|droid]] that served as an automated mechanic, performing a variety of repair duties and often serving as an adjunct or substitute for a [[Navigation computer/Legends|nav computer]] on smaller [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. Astromech droids could also use the mainframes of larger ships to their advantage. Many [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] relied on astromech [[Pilot/Legends|co-pilots]].

==Overview==
{{Quote|You stupid little astro droid!|A B2 super battle droid to R2-D2, moments before being incinerated|audio=YouStupidLittleAstrodroid.flac|<ref name="Episode 3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
An astromech droid's primary purpose on a smaller ship such as a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] was as a backup or replacement for a nav computer; however, due to the limitations of each unit's [[astrogation buffer]], an astromech could only hold a set number of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] coordinates. The droid also provided in-flight maintenance and repair, and performed a number of routine functions so the pilot could focus on flying the ship.

[[File:ThreeArtoos-SWCTP.png|thumb|left|250px|R2-series astromech droids]]

Larger starships usually carried a large complement of these droids in case of malfunctions or combat damage, while some [[Snubfighter/Legends|snubfighters]] (notably the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]] and [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]]) carried a droid in a special port for in-flight field repairs. Astromech droids had, in some cases, also been known to carry out light janitorial duties, and several instances of [[Slicer/Legends|slicing]] carried out by these droids have been known, though this often required the installation of special programming.

Most astromechs were only able to communicate in writing, conveyed via another computer system, or through [[Binary/Legends|binary]], a special code of clicks, bleeps, and similar sounds. Some craft that used astromechs could be equipped with [[astromech translator]]s to facilitate communication.

The term "astromech droid" had been used informally by [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] since around the time of the [[Jedi Civil War]] at least, to refer to the [[Cleaning droid/Legends|utility droids]] that performed similar tasks during that era. It was not until some decades before the beginning of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], when the company [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] started launching its highly successful lines of astromech droids, that the term caught on and started to become synonymous with its models, most notably the [[R-series/Legends|R-series]] of astromech droids, ranging from the [[R1-series astromech droid/Legends|R1-series]] to the [[R9-series astromech droid|R9-series]].

[[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], an Industrial Automaton [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech droid]], was an [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|influential]] unit within the [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].
